The route

Your AI requests a tool. GateRook checks the endpoint policy, resolves credentials locally, and calls the configured service.

Understand the request flow

Ask your AI

Find recent order 48213 errors in AWS CloudWatch Logs and explain the sequence.

logs_search · arguments
{
  "connection": "stage-cloudwatch",
  "query": "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /48213/ and @message like /ERROR/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20",
  "from": "-15m",
  "to": "now",
  "limit": 20
}
Example result
{
  "backend": "cloudwatch",
  "entries": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2026-10-22T12:29:00Z",
      "severity": "ERROR",
      "message": "Payment authorization timed out for order 48213"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "truncated": false
}

Sample configuration and output, not a live connection. Replace example values with your environment. Tool names here are connector names; the endpoint may expose a connection-specific name.

Put context to work

What you can do with AWS CloudWatch Logs and AI

Inspect a service failure

Search the log group of the affected service and correlate messages by order or request identifier, keeping the time window close to the incident.

Investigate a Lambda error

Create a connection scoped to the relevant Lambda log group, then let the AI inspect returned events alongside a separately scoped AWS connection.

Keep log access distinct from infrastructure access

Expose CloudWatch log search without granting the AI general AWS inventory or resource-action tools.

From service to MCP

How to connect AWS CloudWatch Logs

GateRook must be running on a computer that can reach your service. Open Connections, choose Add connection, and select Logs. Give the connection a name and environment.

New to GateRook? Start with the full setup guide.
  1. 01

    Prepare AWS log access

    Choose an existing local AWS profile or provide an access key in GateRook. Ensure the identity can read the selected log groups and run the configured search API. If using AssumeRole, configure the role trust and permissions.

  2. 02

    Set region, groups and credentials

    Open Connections, Add connection and AWS CloudWatch. Enter the region, explicit log groups, credential source and optional role ARN. Keep unrelated groups out of this connection.

  3. 03

    Choose the search language and test

    Select Logs Insights or Filter patterns, then run Test connection and finish Add to endpoint. The example below uses Insights. Start with a short time window and verify the result in Playground.

  4. 04

    Choose the endpoint and tool modes

    Add the tested connection to an endpoint. In Tools & policies, enable only the tools needed for the task. Start with Read only where supported; use Approval for any selected mutation and leave other tools Off. A connection alone does not grant an AI client access.

  5. 05

    Connect your AI and verify the first call

    In Clients, choose your AI app and endpoint, review the connection details, and connect. Try this guide’s example in Playground before asking your AI. Open Activity to inspect the tool, target, decision and returned result. The getting started guide covers this shared flow.

Connection settings

Configure AWS CloudWatch Logs in GateRook

These are example values for the connection form. Enter credentials into GateRook’s secret fields, not into an AI prompt. Requirements and alternatives are noted per field.

AWS CloudWatch Logs connection configuration
SettingExampleHow to use it
Connector typeAWS CloudWatchSelect this Logs variant for log search, rather than the separate AWS infrastructure connector.
Name / environmentstage-cloudwatch / stageA dedicated connection for the selected log groups.
Regioneu-central-1The AWS region containing the configured log groups.
Log groups/services/orders-stageList the log group names or supported log group ARNs the agent may query.
Credentials source / profileprofile / orders-readerThe profile must exist on the GateRook computer. Access-key credentials are also supported.
Role ARNarn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gw-readonlyOptional AssumeRole target. Its trust policy must allow the selected source identity.
Search APIinsightsUse Logs Insights QL; the alternative filter mode expects FilterLogEvents patterns.

Know what you expose

AWS CloudWatch Logs tools and access boundaries

The connector determines what is possible. Endpoint modes and connection policies determine what a particular AI client may use.

Available tools and access behavior
ToolPurposeAccess behavior
logs_searchSearch a bounded time range in the backend query language, with a cursor for older results.Read only
logs_tailRead new log entries since a cursor, waiting up to eight seconds for another page.Read only

Before you enable access

  • This integration reads logs. It does not edit entries, change retention or administer the logging service.
  • The connection scope, environment policy and result limits all apply. A truncated page is only part of the evidence.
  • Log messages may contain application data or sensitive payloads. Scope the source and review the data your AI app is permitted to receive.
  • Logs Insights queries are billed by AWS for scanned data. Narrow the time range and log groups.
  • The query language depends on Search API. A Logs Insights query is not a FilterLogEvents pattern.

GateRook stores local connection secrets encrypted and resolves them for connectors. Allowed tool results are returned to your AI client and may be processed by its provider. Scope the data you expose as well as the actions you allow.

Practical answers

AWS CloudWatch Logs connection questions

Use Test connection to isolate service access problems. Use Playground and Activity to inspect endpoint permissions and tool calls.

Is this the same as the AWS connector?

No. AWS CloudWatch is a Logs backend that exposes logs_search and logs_tail. The separate AWS connector covers its own infrastructure tools.

Can I use an AWS profile instead of pasting a secret key?

Yes. Select profile as the credentials source and specify a profile available on the computer running GateRook. Optional role assumption uses that source identity.

Will a query search my entire AWS account?

The connection has an explicit region and log group list. Keep that list narrow; tool calls can also target a configured source.
